keyTerms.definition: Unit 05 of CS229S, covering quantization and sparsity.
The evidence label on every lesson claim, here PLANNED with source attribution pending.

recall.question: What unit and session anchor this lesson?
recall.answer: Unit cs229s-U05, concepts C01 to C12, calendar-anchored to Week 4, Oct 14, Memory Efficient Neural Networks.

keyTerms.definition: The fixed structure every concept carries, from source and scope to visual units.
Quantization and sparsity are taught as algorithms with computed error.

recall.question: Do the labs need a GPU?
recall.answer: No: quantization and sparsity are taught as algorithms with computed error, no GPU needed for the labs.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: 16 evenly spaced marks standing in for floats.
s = (max - min) / (2^b - 1): the spacing between marks.
Stretch s and crush the small values onto one level.

recall.question: Write s, z, x_q, x_hat.
recall.answer: s = (max - min)/(2^b - 1). z = round(-min/s). x_q = clamp(round(x/s) + z). x_hat = s*(x_q - z).

recall.question: min=-1, max=1, b=4. Quantize 0.5 and -0.25. Give x_hat and error.
Many small values map to one level. Name the cause.
recall.answer: Outliers: one weight at 100 with the rest in [-1, 1] makes s = 0.396, crushing values under 0.2. Clip or use per-channel.

keyTerms.definition: Bounded by s/2 for values inside [min, max].
Unbounded: outside the range, values snap to the edge.

recall.question: Bound the rounding error.
recall.answer: For x in [min, max]: |x - x_hat| <= s/2.

recall.question: s = 0.1333. Max rounding error. Clipping error for x = 2.0?
recall.answer: Max rounding error 0.0667. x = 2.0 clips to x_hat = 0.9333, error 1.0667.

recall.question: MSE high, max error huge. Which error dominates?
recall.answer: Clipping: rounding is bounded by s/2, clipping grows with distance past the edge.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: one thermostat for the whole house vs one per room.
One (s, z) per output channel: each channel gets its own ruler.
One (s, z) per group of g elements (e.g. g = 128).

recall.question: Define the three granularities.
recall.answer: Per-tensor: one (s, z) for the whole tensor. Per-channel: one per output channel. Per-group: one per group of g elements.

recall.question: Rows [-100,100], [-1,1], 4-bit. Per-tensor s and the fate of row 2?
recall.answer: s = 13.33. Row 2's values all snap to ~one level: destroyed.

recall.question: Per-tensor int8 fails quality. First change?
recall.answer: Go per-channel for weights (almost always the right first move).

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: weights packed at the factory (static), activations at the gate (dynamic).
W in int8, activations fp16: the matmul dequantizes on the fly.
Per-batch (s, z) from the batch's min/max: tracks the data.

recall.question: Define weight-only vs W8A8.
recall.answer: Weight-only: W int8, activations fp16. W8A8: both int8, integer matmul accumulating in int32.

recall.question: W (4096, 4096) fp32 vs int8. Traffic bytes?
recall.answer: fp32: 67,108,864 bytes. int8: 16,777,216 bytes: 4x less.

recall.question: Static int8 fails on new data. Explain and fix.
recall.answer: The new domain shifts activations outside the calibrated range: clipping explodes. Recalibrate or go dynamic.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: fit the ruler to the crowd, clip the giant.
Range from [p0.05, p99.95]: fits the bulk, clips outliers.

recall.question: Name three range-picking methods.
recall.answer: Min/max, percentile, and MSE search over candidate ranges.

recall.question: 9999 values in [-1,1], one at 1000. s for min/max and 99.9 percentile?
recall.answer: Min/max: s = 3.925. 99.9 percentile: s ~ 0.0078.

recall.question: Calibrated int8 fails in prod. Name the mismatch.
recall.answer: Calibration data does not match deployment. Monitor and recalibrate.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: unstructured zeros are free choice, 2:4 is assigned seating the usher can plan.
In each group of 4, exactly 2 nonzero: sparse tensor cores skip fast.

recall.question: Define 2:4, block, unstructured.
recall.answer: 2:4: exactly 2 nonzero per group of 4. Block: all-or-nothing bxb tiles. Unstructured: arbitrary zeros, needs indices.

recall.question: 8 weights, 4 zeros. Which patterns are 2:4-valid?
recall.answer: [1,0,0,1,0,1,1,0] is valid (2 nonzeros per group). [1,1,1,1,0,0,0,0] is not.

recall.question: 50% sparse, no speedup. Name the pattern problem.
recall.answer: Unstructured: index overhead eats the math saving (~1x). The pattern decides, not the count.

keyTerms.definition: Zero out the smallest |w|: cut the thinnest branches.
Loss change per weight on removal: the exact-ish pruning score.

recall.question: Define magnitude pruning in one line.
recall.answer: Zero out the smallest |w| per layer or globally.

recall.question: W = [0.1, 2.0, -0.05, 1.5], prune 50%. Mask and pruned W?
90% magnitude prune collapses. Two fixes?
recall.answer: Sensitivity-guided pruning, or gradual pruning (prune a little, retrain, repeat).

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: skipping zeros saves steps, but index lookups are tolls.
The per-nonzero index lookup that costs unstructured sparsity its win.

recall.question: Write the realized-time formula.
recall.answer: Time = math_time / speedup + index_overhead; realized(dense, sparsity, gather_frac) = dense * ((1 - sparsity) + gather_frac).

recall.question: Dense 100 us, 50% sparse, gather 45 us. Speedup?
2:4 kernel at 1.0x. Name two causes.
recall.answer: Shapes do not qualify for tensor cores, or the gather overhead is not the 2:4 path (wrong kernel).

keyTerms.definition: B = B_1 ... B_k with k = log2(n): full mixing at O(n log n).
The mental model: each factor pairs up entries and mixes them.
Butterfly parameter count vs n^2 dense.

recall.question: Write the parameter count.
recall.answer: k = log2(n) factors, 2n per factor: 2n log n total.

recall.question: n = 1024. Dense vs butterfly params?
recall.answer: Dense about 1M (1,048,576). Butterfly 20,480: 51x fewer.

recall.question: Butterfly fit has huge error. Explain.
recall.answer: Not every matrix factorizes this way: learn the factors, do not assume universality.

keyTerms.definition: M = P L P^T R: two block-diagonal factors plus permutations.
The mental model: permute into districts, mix inside, permute back, mix across.
P routes information across blocks.

recall.question: Write the Monarch form and param count.
recall.answer: M = P L P^T R. Block size b: O(nb) per factor, O(2nb) for the pair.

recall.question: n = 4096, b = 256. Params vs dense?
recall.answer: 2 * 4096 * 256 = 2.1M vs 16.7M dense: 8x fewer.

recall.question: Monarch underfits. Explain.
recall.answer: Structured factors are harder to optimize: fewer degrees of freedom, worse conditioning. Tune the optimizer.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: each layer adds its error and passes previous errors along, amplified.
L_i of each layer: the per-layer amplification factor.

recall.question: Write the error bound.
recall.answer: Total <= sum_i e_i * prod_{j>i} L_j.

recall.question: errs 0.01 x2, lips 1.5, 1.0. Bound?
First-layer int8 kills quality, last-layer int8 fine. Explain.
recall.answer: Early-layer errors are amplified by all later layers. Keep early layers precise.

keyTerms.definition: The mental model: perplexity is one gauge, task evals are the road.
Perplexity delta, task accuracy deltas, latency/throughput targets.
Step 5 of the protocol: canary the compressed model in prod.

recall.question: Name the three gates.
recall.answer: Perplexity delta, task accuracy deltas, latency/throughput targets.

recall.question: ppl +0.8%, task +0, lat 12 ms. Ship?
recall.answer: Ship: all three gates pass.

recall.question: ppl flat, task down. What does this prove about the gate?
recall.answer: Perplexity under-gates: a flat perplexity can hide a broken long-range task. Run the task suite.

keyTerms.definition: The unit's bottom line: shrink the bytes, prove the quality.
int8 weights, 2:4 kernels, structured layers: the right side of the plate.

recall.question: What does the unit chapter plate contrast?
recall.answer: Naive view (fp32 dense, full traffic) vs the compressed system (int8 weights, 2:4 kernels, structured layers). Bottom line: shrink the bytes, prove the quality.

keyTerms.definition: The Shell 3 rule: x_q = clamp(round(x/s) + z).
Zero maps to zero, in-range error <= s/2.

recall.question: What is the Shell 3 rule of the linear-quantization ladder?
recall.answer: x_q = clamp(round(x/s) + z).

recall.question: What breaks the ladder (Shell 7)?
recall.answer: Breaking the range (outlier): the quiet channel dies.

keyTerms.definition: C12: the deployment checklist for every compressed model.
C11: tells the LLM engineer which layers keep their bits.

recall.question: What are the MLOps deployment checklist items for a compressed model?
recall.answer: The three gates (C12): perplexity delta, task accuracy deltas, latency/throughput targets.
